title: streaming event-delegation & sink adapter ergonomics for python sdk
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a developer-friendly set of primitives for Python SDK streaming chat completions that separate event handling (delegates) from finalization sinks. Goals: make common flows (incremental UI updates, resumable consumers, fanout to analytics) easy, pluggable, and debuggable without leaking runtime internals.
acceptance_criteria: Public API exposes a lightweight EventDelegate protocol that receives typed events (token, delta, done, error, meta) and can be composed with sinks
Provide at least three sink adapters: MemoryAccumulator (for sync testing), AsyncIteratorSink (resume-friendly), and FileCheckpointSink (durable checkpoints) with clear example usage
Retry semantics integrated: idempotency token handling + transparent soft-retry policy for transient network errors with developer hooks for backoff and telemetry
Comprehensive examples in examples/streaming: incremental-chat-widget.py, resumable-consumer-demo.py, analytics-fanout.py
Automated tests covering partial-stream recovery, duplicate-event suppression, and backpressure behavior under load
Docs page (console + repo README) explaining composition patterns and recommended defaults for production (batching, checkpoint frequency, retention)
notes: Motivation: many integrators reimplement small pieces (checkpointing, fanout, idempotency) and get subtle bugs when combining retries + resume
Trade-offs considered: heavy async-only API vs unified sync/async facade. We propose ergonomic wrappers that allow sync testing while offering async-first performance path.
Security: sinks that persist checkpoints will be optional and documented; recommend using KMS-backed stores for production persistence (link to infra-guidance)
